title: security: RBAC v2 residency + KMS audit hardening (region pinning enforcement)
author: Priya Nair
body:
Motivation: Enforce RBAC v2 residency and KMS region pinning and improve audit logging to meet customer compliance requirements. This PR hardens the enforcement path (previously audit-only), adds explicit audit entries for KMS residency checks, and plugs a gap where region-pinned keys could be used with mismatched compute regions. Includes migration helpers for existing policies and rollout steps for canary verification.

Summary of changes: consolidated RBAC residency checks into the new residency middleware; KMS client now validates key-region metadata before signing; audit-logger emits an "action=residency_check" event with key metadata and decision; new configuration flag rbac.enforce_residency toggles enforcement (default: true for next release); migration CLI (rbac-migrate-residency) converts legacy residency annotations to RBAC v2 policies; unit and e2e tests added for edge cases (cross-region key alias, fallback policies).

Checklist:
- [x] RBAC middleware enforcement and unit tests
- [x] KMS region validation + integration tests against mock KMS
- [x] Audit events emitted for each decision and logged with request context
- [x] Migration helper and docs update
- [x] Canary rollout plan and feature flag gating

Notes on rollout: feature gated behind rbac.enforce_residency and a runtime canary cohort. We will enable audit-only mode for 48 hours, review aggregated audit logs for false positives, then flip to enforcement for the cohort, then expand. See linked Linear ENG-8421 for phased plan.

Security considerations: This tightens existing behavior and may surface policy gaps for tenants who relied on cross-region keys. Migration helper aims to reduce manual work. Operations should contact security@redwood.ai before enabling enforcement in dedicated/private deployments.

Backwards compatibility: No API surface changes. Configuration default will be enforce=true for the next minor release per SEC roadmap; customers can opt-out temporarily.

Files changed (high level): updated rbac middleware, kms client validation, audit logger, migration CLI, several unit/integration tests, docs and release notes.

References: Linear ENG-8421, SEC-1102, Jira SUP-4521.

review_comments: Carlos Mendes: Left a few nits around log message formats and a question about high-cardinality fields in audit events. Please remove PII and use redaction helper.
Priya Nair (author): Thanks — addressed in latest commit, normalized audit fields via audit/logger/serializer.go and added tests for redaction.
Hannah Lee: Can you add a short migration note for Dedicated customers? They might need to rotate keys if they intentionally used cross-region keys. Also flag ops to run canary during low traffic.
Priya Nair: Added dedicated-deploy notes in docs and added a canary checklist in the changelog. Ops notified in SEC-1102 thread.

Omar Farouk: Verified integration tests locally against mock KMS; tests look good. +1 pending CI. Consider adding an informational metric for number of denied requests due to residency for 2 weeks post-rollout.
Priya Nair: Added metric rbac.residency.denied_count and dashboard stub in observability; will follow up with a dashboard PR.
ci_summary: Security scan: pass (SNYK: no critical findings)
Performance: marginal regressed token path in a microbenchmark (3%); flagged to perf team in ENG-8435

Ops runbook updated in docs/security/residency.md with canary checklist
Feature flag rbac.enforce_residency default toggled to true in next release; backport plan created for dedicated customers
release_notes: Security: Enforce RBAC v2 residency for KMS keys and emit audit events for residency decisions. Added migration helper (rbac-migrate-residency) and observability for denied residency checks. Default enforcement will be enabled in the next minor release; see docs/security/residency.md for rollout steps.
notes_for_support: Customers who relied on cross-region KMS keys may see request denials after enforcement. Recommend running rbac-migrate-residency --dry-run to inspect affected resources and coordinate key rotations. Support/ops: contact security@redwood.ai for exemptions.
